label: Predynastic / Early Dynastic
description: The earliest Egyptian religion. The gods Ra, Osiris, Isis, Horus, Set, and others are worshipped. The earliest evidence is archaeological (tombs, offerings, early inscriptions).

label: Old Kingdom
description: The Pyramid Texts are inscribed in the pyramids — the earliest surviving religious texts. They describe the king's journey to the sky and his union with the gods.

label: Middle Kingdom
description: The 'Contendings of Horus and Set' and other mythic texts are composed. The Book of the Dead begins to take shape.

label: New Kingdom
description: The Book of the Dead (in its classic form) is used. Amun rises to supreme status (Amun-Ra). The great temples at Karnak and Luxor are built.

label: Late / Ptolemaic
description: The 'Isis cult' spreads across the Mediterranean. The last temple (at Philae) closes in 395 CE under the Roman/Christian empire.
